example.scenario: Publicly exposed AWS S3 bucket containing sensitive customer PII data was discovered by an external researcher using automated scanning, leading to unauthorized data download.

technical_data.http_request:
GET /customers/2023/PII_export_20230515.csv HTTP/1.1
Host: customer-data-backup-prod.s3.amazonaws.com
User-Agent: aws-sdk-go/1.34.0 (go1.15.2; linux; amd64)
Accept-Encoding: identity
technical_data.downloaded_file_snippet:
customer_id,full_name,email,ssn,phone,address
12345,John Doe,john.doe@example.com,987-65-4320,555-123-4567,"123 Elm St, Springfield, IL"
67890,Jane Smith,jane.smith@example.com,123-45-6789,555-987-6543,"456 Oak St, Metropolis, NY"

indicators: CloudTrail logs showing anonymous GetObject requests
S3 bucket policy allowing principal '*' to GetObject on sensitive bucket
HTTP GET requests from suspicious IPs targeting S3 bucket objects
Downloaded CSV file containing PII data with direct unauthenticated access
Use of --no-sign-request in AWS CLI to access public buckets
example.detection_method: Automated monitoring of CloudTrail logs for anonymous or public GetObject calls, alerting on S3 buckets with public read policies, integration with AWS Config rules to enforce bucket ACLs and policies limiting public access, anomaly detection on unusual access patterns or IP geolocations, and regular bucket inventory and vulnerability scanning.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1078 - Valid Accounts (anonymous access via public bucket)
T1560.001 - Archive Collected Data: Archive via Cloud Storage
T1537 - Transfer Data to Cloud Account

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents the problem of misconfigured cloud storage leading to unauthorized data access. The scenario clearly describes a publicly exposed AWS S3 bucket containing sensitive PII data accessed anonymously, which aligns well with the problem nature. The technical data includes realistic CloudTrail logs showing anonymous GetObject events, the exact misconfigured IAM and bucket policies allowing public read access, HTTP request details, and evidence of downloaded sensitive data. The indicators explicitly connect the technical evidence to the problem, explaining why the sample matches the misconfiguration and exposure issue. The detection methods are comprehensive and appropriate for risk reduction, including automated monitoring, alerting, AWS Config integration, anomaly detection, and scanning. The inclusion of relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques further supports the scenario's realism and completeness. All required fields are present and well populated, making this a complete and plausible example for the stated cybersecurity problem.
